deliverables: Upgrade Cardano mainnet protocol from version 10.0 to 11.0 while remaining in the Conway era.
Make new Plutus primitives from CIP-0109, CIP-0132, CIP-0133, CIP-0138, and CIP-0153 available.
Make all Plutus built-in functions available consistently across Plutus V1, V2, and V3.
Add UPLC case expressions for Bool, Integer, and Data.
Enforce VRF key hash uniqueness at the ledger level and promote or tighten several ledger validation predicates.
Improve Cardano node PPView mismatch reporting.
request.what: Initiate an intra-era Cardano mainnet hard fork to Protocol Version 11 minor 0, named the van Rossem hard fork.

claims.claim: The proposal would upgrade Cardano mainnet to protocol version 11.0 through an intra-era hard fork while remaining in the Conway era.
The hard fork would introduce Plutus primitives defined in CIP-0109, CIP-0132, CIP-0133, CIP-0138, and CIP-0153, including modular exponentiation, dropList, BLS12-381 MSM, Array, and Value built-ins.
All Plutus built-in functions, including newly introduced ones, would become available across Plutus V1, V2, and V3.
UPLC case expressions over Bool, Integer, and Data would improve script performance and produce cleaner script logic.
The upgrade would preserve all other Protocol Version 10 functionality and leave transaction shape unchanged, minimizing ecosystem upgrade effort.

Testing reports demonstrate no behavioral regressions, complete specification-to-implementation conformance for new ledger rules, and correct operation of new Plutus primitives and case expressions across Plutus V1, V2, and V3.
Security audits have been undertaken for Plutus BLS primitives and execution costs for all Plutus primitives.

A linked Cardano Node 11.0.1 performance report shows no regressions for standard value, Plutus, and voting benchmarks and acceptable baseline performance for new Plutus primitives and case expressions.

The proposal states it is consistent with all eight cited hard fork guardrails, while HARDFORK-04 requires verification that at least 85% of stake pools by active stake have upgraded before ratification.

Reversion after the hard fork would only be possible in extreme circumstances through the CIP-0135 disaster recovery process, though companion cost model settings could be changed if Plutus primitive issues are discovered.

summary: The document requests a Cardano hard fork to protocol version 11.0 with no treasury withdrawal, centered on Plutus capability and performance changes, ledger predicate tightening, node diagnostics, and guardrail consistency subject to stake pool readiness verification.
